reason: This text fragment from 2 Samuel 13 describes a private family incident involving Amnon's sexual assault of Tamar. While King David hears of these events and becomes angry ('וַיִּחַר לוֹ מְאֹד' - 'and he was very angry'), his anger is directed at his son Amnon's heinous actions toward his daughter, not at any complaint about the people of Israel. The narrative contains no reference to Hebrew leaders complaining about the people, nor does it involve any complaint about the general population or subjects.
